papers.title_en: When Flaws Cascade: Understanding Vulnerabilities and Exploitation Chains in JavaScript Engines
papers.authors: Yuhan Ma, Jiongchi Yu, Xiaofei Xie, Qiang Hu, Zhiyi Zhang, Junjie Wang
papers.evidence: JavaScript引擎漏洞与利用链的实证研究
papers.tldr: JavaScript引擎是现代浏览器核心，但复杂性与广泛部署使其成为攻击目标；现有研究多聚焦漏洞检测，缺乏对其特征与可利用性的系统理解。本文开展首个针对JavaScript引擎漏洞的综合性实证研究，构建2017—2024年四大主流引擎的241个漏洞数据集。通过深入分析，建立症状与根因分类法，并识别利用前提、提取从逻辑错误到内存安全违规的漏洞触发链，同时分析缓解策略。研究为开发者与研究者提供可操作安全启示。
papers.abstract_en: JavaScript engines are pivotal to modern web browsers, enabling the execution of dynamic and interactive web applications. However, their complexity and widespread adoption make them prime targets for attackers exploiting vulnerabilities. While existing research has focused on detecting vulnerabilities of JavaScript engines, a significant gap remains in systematically understanding the characteristics of these vulnerabilities, including their symptoms, root causes, and exploitability. This paper bridges this gap by presenting the first comprehensive empirical study on vulnerabilities in JavaScript engines, investigating their characteristics and potential exploitation strategies.   We construct a dataset comprising 241 vulnerabilities across four mainstream JavaScript engines from 2017 to 2024. Through in-depth analysis, we first develop taxonomies for symptoms and root causes. Building on this understanding, we investigate the exploitability of these vulnerabilities, identifying key prerequisites and extracting vulnerability trigger chains that demonstrate how logical errors propagate into memory safety violations. Additionally, we analyze the mitigation strategies to counter these exploits. Finally, we summarize key implications for various stakeholders, including developers and researchers, offering actionable insights to improve the security and resilience of JavaScript engines.

papers.title_en: A Resilient Runtime-Verification Fabric for Security Monitoring of Critical Edge-IoT Infrastructure
papers.authors: Nikolaos Kekatos, Marinelio Chintri, Panagiotis Katsaros, Alexios Lekidis, Tom Nianios, Ioannis Seitoglou, Anastasios Temperekidis, Stylianos Basagiannis
papers.evidence: 面向IoT机群运行时安全监控的弹性运行时验证架构
papers.tldr: 关键边缘IoT基础设施的运行时验证常依赖单机原型共享日志，崩溃、时钟偏移、网络静默和慢消费者会静默丢事件，监控器仍对损坏视图输出结论。RV-Fabric用MQTT与持久流代理构建弹性交付层，恢复崩溃持久交付、可信事件顺序、全静默下进展、消费者隔离与限流五项连续性保证，并把证据完整性写入验证语义。故障注入下共享日志基线漏报7起事件中的6起，RV-Fabric全部保留。
papers.abstract_en: Protecting critical infrastructure increasingly depends on continuously verifying large IoT fleets against formal security specifications at runtime. Yet the runtime-verification (RV) pipelines proposed for this task are typically single-host prototypes whose monitors read a shared log file, with no resilience to the failures such deployments incur: a crash or overload silently drops events, clock skew corrupts the ordering metric monitors require, a time-triggered "node has gone silent" property cannot fire when the network itself falls silent, and one slow consumer stalls the pipeline. Each failure is silent: the monitor keeps emitting verdicts over a corrupted view. We present RV-Fabric, a resilient delivery layer that carries the hierarchy over two brokers (MQTT for device ingest, a durable stream broker for backend delivery) and re-establishes five continuity guarantees: durable delivery under crashes, a trusted event order, progress under total silence, consumer isolation and flow control under bounded overload, each an invariant conditioned on broker durability. Above the transport, RV-Fabric makes evidence completeness part of runtime-verification semantics: every verdict carries a status (sound, degraded, incomplete or unavailable) derived from delivery gaps, retention pressure and liveness, so an incomplete stream cannot yield an unqualified all-clear. Under controlled fault injection on a containerised testbed, measured against a fault-free oracle using the real MonPoly engine, the shared-log baseline misses six of seven injected incidents, reporting each as an unqualified all-clear, whereas RV-Fabric preserves all seven; removing a delivery mechanism reintroduces silent loss, removing isolation costs only timeliness. Two published critical-infrastructure datasets, water-SCADA and IoT/IIoT, replay end-to-end.
